title.rendered: Anita Joseph, Caramel Plug trade words over stolen photo

content.rendered:
Actress, Anita Joseph, has found herself at the centre of an online controversy after publicly apologising to social media personality, Ogechi Ukonu, popularly known as Caramel Plug, over a doctored photograph.

The apology came after Caramel Plug accused the actress of using artificial intelligence to swap faces in one of her original photographs before posting it as her own. The incident sparked conversations about authenticity, content ownership and the growing use of artificial intelligence in content creation.

The drama began on Thursday when Caramel shared side-by-side images on Instagram, expressing shock over the disputed photograph. In the image, Joseph appeared wearing a brown blazer, waistcoat, tie and yellow heels, but with her face digitally superimposed on Caramel Plug’s body.

Accusing the actress of altering her original photograph, Caramel wrote, “You don’t even follow me on any socials, we don’t know each other. Anita, you removed my head from my picture and inserted yours before posting it publicly.”

The post quickly gained traction, with many social media users criticising Joseph’s action and describing it as unethical.

In response, Joseph deleted the controversial post and apologised.

“I cannot even be caught up in this kind of mess. Sorry babe. It was my AI boy, this guy wan implicate me,” she wrote.

While some social media users “accepted” the apology, others questioned the explanation, arguing that the actress should have verified the image before sharing it or sought permission from its original owner.

Joseph also maintained that her intention was to promote the outfit featured in the photograph.

“You see why I don’t like dis AI thing… na where I wan help person promote him work oo,” she added.

Caramel Plug, however, dismissed the explanation, replying, “Lol, okay. Please ensure your imaginary AI boy does better next time. Secondly, I’m not your baby, I really don’t know you.”

Joseph responded, “Nobody knew you took a picture like that, girl. I made you trend.”

The controversy took another turn after actress, Angela Okorie, weighed in, criticising Joseph’s actions.

Describing the incident as “yeyebrity behaviour”, Okorie said, “What is bad is bad. Removing someone’s head from their picture to replace it with yours is wrong. No celebrity should ever do something like that.”

Joseph also fired back at Okorie, threatening legal action.

“You are out of your cage again. I will arrest you and you won’t come out,” she wrote.

Caramel Plug, meanwhile, maintained her stance, warning against the unauthorised use of her content in the future.
